newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firm, trade cautious before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firm, trade cautious before FOMC.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to keep a firm tone on Monday, but trade may be subdued ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's policy-setting meeting on Tuesday, brokers said.

They also said the Tokyo stock market would be supported by strong demand from foreign investors and domestic pension funds, but the yen's strength and Friday's sharp fall in Wall Street stocks would inhibit rises in the Nikkei average.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 268.42 points or 1.34 percent to finish at 20,324.73. Its June futures jumped 310 points to 20,370.
"The Nikkei 225 is likely to head towards 20,500," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

The market has been supported by an inflow of funds from investors, who do not expect any more crisis in the Japanese financial system and who have brightened their outlook for the Japanese economy, brokers said.
But some brokers said the trade could be subdued on Monday, with the U.S. interest rate outlook unclear.
"Many people are likely to take a wait-and-see stance ahead of the FOMC meeting," said a broker at a medium-sized securities house.
Market participants are worried if the Fed tightens its monetary stance, this could hurt U.S. stocks which in turn could have a negative impact on the Tokyo market.
On Friday, the Dow industrials fell 139 points, or 1.89 percent, to 7,195 on renewed fears that the Fed will raise short term interest rates.
